title: Conversions and defaults
description:
Write three functions:

```javascript
function toNumber(text) { }                     // the number in text, or null if it is not a number
function volumeOr(volume, fallback) { }         // volume, unless it is null or undefined (0 is a real volume!)
function setting(user, key, fallback) { }       // user.settings[key], or fallback when anything on the way is missing
```

`toNumber` ignores spaces around the number and accepts decimals and a minus sign, but returns `null` for an empty or blank text and for anything that `Number` cannot convert (such as `"4x"`).
hints: `Number("")` is `0`, not `NaN`: check for blank text first. `text.trim()` removes the spaces at both ends (lesson 1.04), so `if (text.trim() === "") return null;` handles empty and blank text (`if` runs the `return` only when the condition is true; lesson 1.05). `Number.isNaN(n)` detects a failed conversion.
`a?.b?.[key]` stops at the first `null` or `undefined` and gives `undefined`; `?? fallback` then supplies the default.
